state.decision: Two choices made while rebuilding the Editor header to the new Figma design (24 Nov 2026), put to Jev and Laya after the fact.
state.facts: The old header had a brand, two scene identity inputs, eight file and edit buttons (New, Open, Import SVG, Save, Undo, Redo, History, Reset layout) and a tool ribbon. The design has a 28 px menu bar with a context line at its right, and a 40 px ribbon with tools, an engine chip, undo, redo and a Publish button; it has no file buttons in the bar. Every one of those file buttons already has a menu item (File and Edit menus) that runs the very same element by clicking it, so the elements must stay in the page. The scene has no field saying whether a project is progressive or interlaced (that is plan row 7.8, not built); the design's context line reads 1080p50.
state.built: The file buttons stay in the page, hidden; their jobs are the menu items. Undo and redo move to the ribbon. The context line reads the size and the rate (1920x1080 . 50 fps) and says no scan.

file_buttons.instructions: What should happen to the file buttons that every menu item already duplicates?

criteria.A: Hide them from the bar and keep the elements so the menu items still run them; the design has no such buttons.
criteria.B: Keep them visible in the bar beside the new ribbon controls.
criteria.C: Delete the elements and rewrite the menu items to call the code directly.

scan.instructions: The design's context line says 1080p50, but the contract does not yet record whether a project is progressive or interlaced. What should the line say?

criteria.A: The size and the rate without a scan letter: 1920x1080, 50 fps; add the letter when the contract records it.
criteria.C: Leave the format out of the line.
